results.content: # [What is the difference between Sprint and Iteration in Scrum and length of each Sprint? [closed]](/questions/1227318/what-is-the-difference-between-sprint-and-iteration-in-scrum-and-length-of-each). For exampole we can have a sprint of a week ad an iteration of a week. A sprint is normally an iteration. Iteration is synonymous with sprint, sprint is just the Scrum terminology. Once again, varying the sprint length reduces your teams ability to provide that velocity statistic which the team uses for sprint planning, and the product owner uses for release planning (i.e. predicting when the project will end or what will be in the project at the end). 1. Where I work we have 2 Sprints to an Iteration. 1. Sprint is just the term for an iteration. 2. You can change the Sprint length to be anything you want, but likely you'll want to try to find an amount of time that "works well" (which may mean any number of things for your team) and end up sticking with it over time.

results.title: Azure Devops picking the "wrong" sprint to show in Sprint board
results.content: Earlier, when we had a "flat" list of our sprints / iterations, Azure Devops would also jump to the "correct" sprint as the "current" sprint and display it - based on the "from" and "to" dates of that sprint. Is there any way we can *tell* Azure Devops to *ignore* the top-level PI entries, and just find the correct sprint in the list of "child iterations" for a PI entry? As long as "PI 5" is not assigned to the team, it should not show up in the sprints dropdown and not be picked up as "current iteration". In other words, even with the above set-up that I have shared, teams can still assign a Feature or an Epic or whatever work item you use to the "PI 6" iteration path node and you can run queries against "PI 6" etc. 1") Azure DevOps boards missing sprints/iterations.
